subject: POC packaging: time extension vs small commit + SKU swap
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira.patel@novocorp.com>
To: david_kim@redwood-inference.com
Cc: Alan Chu <alan.chu@novocorp.com>, procurement@novocorp.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC wrap / next steps - question on extension vs commit

Hi David,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the Redwood demo helped our infra and product teams validate the latency and token-cost assumptions. We’re close to an internal go/no-go but need two quick asks before we present to finance next week:

1) If we extend the POC by 4 weeks, what’s the simplest commercial framing? We’d prefer a time-boxed extension (same engagement team) but finance is asking for a single-line cost.

2) Alternatively, would a small, short-term commit (e.g., $30k) get us a reduced rate during the extension window? We’re open to SKU/packaging swaps if that makes implementation easier.

Scope: no new features, same dataset/sample load as last 14 days.

Can you put two short options in writing — time-box price vs commit discount — so I can take them into procurement? If you have a sample SOW amendment, that would help.

Best,
Samira
Samira Patel
Head of Product 
Novocorp

Attachments: none
From: david_kim@redwood-inference.com
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@novocorp.com>
Cc: Alan Chu <alan.chu@novocorp.com>, procurement@novocorp.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC wrap / next steps - question on extension vs commit

Hi Samira,

Appreciate the clear ask — see two pragmatic options below. I’ve attached a one-page pricing options PDF and a draft mutual action plan to speed legal/procurement review.

Option A — Time-box extension (simplest):
- 4-week extension (same scope, same engineering support)
- Fixed fee: $18,000 (flat, covers bursts up to the same max concurrency as current POC)
- SLA: best-effort, priority during business hours; no changes to data retention or logs
- Amendment: simple SOW addendum (one page)

Option B — Short-term commit + discounted unit pricing (better unit economics if you plan to convert):
- 30-day commitment of $30,000, applied to usage during the extension
- Effective token rate: 12% discount vs standard POC rates; includes access to a burst SKU for short higher-concurrency windows (pre-approved by Redwood ops)
- If you convert to Dedicated within 90 days, credit of unused portion up to $8k toward the onboarding fee

Notes:
- If procurement needs invoice lines vs a single flat fee, we can send a T&M-style invoice for Option A or a prepay invoice for Option B.
- We can do either with a one-paragraph amendment / DocuSign.

I’ll loop in Marissa on the discount ask for approval — quick internal check: is 12% off feasible for a $30k commit or should we cap at 10%?

Best,
David Kim
Senior Account Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachments: POC_pricing_options.pdf, Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.docx
From: david_kim@redwood-inference.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, soojin_lee@redwood-inference.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: POC wrap / next steps - question on extension vs commit

Marissa / Soojin — quick internal: Novocorp asked for either a 4‑week time extension ($18k) or a $30k short commit with a discount. Thoughts on the max discount we can offer and whether we should require the success metric clause for conversion credits?

I recommend: 10% off for finance simplicity + include a short success metric (50k calls of inference or 5% reduction in latency for 95th pct) to trigger the $8k credit on conversion. This avoids open-ended credits but signals good will.

Marissa — legal said earlier they’d prefer a single amendment with an explicit scope and no change to data handling. If 10% is okay, I’ll send Option B with that discount; otherwise I’ll stick to Option A flat extension.

Thanks,
David

On Tue, Sep 7, 2026 at 11:05 AM David Kim <david_kim@redwood-inference.com> wrote:
> (see above)
From: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
To: david_kim@redwood-inference.com, soojin_lee@redwood-inference.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: POC wrap / next steps - question on extension vs commit

David — 10% is fine for this motion given the $30k commit and short timeframe. Agree on a concrete success metric to avoid ambiguity. My ask: include a clause that credits are only redeemable if there is an active conversion discussion (email thread or MQL) within 90 days — this protects us from open liabilities.

If finance pushes back, we can also offer a 5% stacking for a one-year evaluation follow-on, but leave that out of the initial amendment.

Marissa
Director, GTM Deals | Redwood Inference
From: Alan Chu <alan.chu@novocorp.com>
To: david_kim@redwood-inference.com
Cc: Samira Patel <samira.patel@novocorp.com>, procurement@novocorp.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC wrap / next steps - question on extension vs commit

David — thanks for laying out options. Novocorp is inclined to take Option A (time-box) for simplicity but asks whether you’ll pro-rate if we only use 3 of the 4 weeks. Procurement also asked whether we can get the price split into two invoice lines (services / burst credits).

If you can pro-rate unused full weeks and provide two invoice lines, we can execute quickly. Otherwise we’ll move to Option B (commit).

Can you send the amendment + DocuSign link? Procurement is on standby.

—Alan
Alan Chu
Sr. Procurement Manager | Novocorp

Alan / Samira — confirmed and thanks. Plan below and next steps:

Final commercial: Option A (time-box) with pro-rata and split invoice
- 4-week extension fee: $18,000 total
- Invoice lines: Services: $15,000; Burst credits: $3,000
- Pro-rate: unused full weeks refunded at $4,000/week (applies only if you terminate early and we’ve not consumed burst credits)
- Amendment: one‑paragraph SOW addendum and a short table of scope — no change to data handling or retention.

Execution steps (DocuSign + MLP):
1) I’ve uploaded the amendment and generated a DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.net/ENVELOPEID/ABCDEF123456
2) HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/78910 (NOVO-POC-2026-09)
3) Redwood ops will reserve the burst SKU during the extension window; Samira, please confirm preferred start date (we recommend start on Mon 2026-09-27 to avoid a partial week).

If procurement prefers the commit option instead, we’ll revert to the previously proposed $30k commitment with a 10% discount and the conversion credit clause.

Thanks — I’ll watch for the signed DocuSign and will kick off the ops booking once we receive it.

Best,
David Kim
